growth.juvenile_note: Seeds sprout in spring on bare mineral soil or burned ground; first-year seedlings are only 5-12 cm tall with small, coarsely toothed oval leaves. Saplings are slender whips with dark reddish-brown, shiny, lenticelled bark; the chalk-white papery bark appears only as stems thicken. After fire or cutting, stumps sprout clumps of several stems.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 2 (Safford et al.): first-year seedlings 5-12 cm, site index 12-24 m at 50 yr, height growth stops at 60-70 yr, few live beyond 140-200 yr, shade-intolerant, reddish-brown sapling bark; USDA FEIS Betula papyrifera.

fruiting.source: USDA Silvics (flowers mid-Apr to early Jun; male catkins 4-10 cm, female 2.5-5 cm; seed from age 15, optimum 40-70; good crops every other year; seeds ripen Aug-mid Sep, 90-95% shed Sep-Nov, some into spring); counts are catkins, estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with 5-7 cotyledons; in its first year it has single, flat, finely serrated primary needles 2-3 cm long, then short, twisted, blue-green paired needles. Young trees are regular, bushy cones; later the lower branches drop and the crown becomes flat or rounded above a tall trunk whose upper bark is orange and flaky.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 35 m, over 45 m on the best sites; normally lives 150-300 years, over 760 in Lapland; first-year seedlings have single serrated leaves 2-3 cm; seeds released 22-24 months after pollination); growth and first cones from European yield tables

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (pollen released mid to late spring; first-year conelets globose, 4-8 mm; mature cones 3-7.5 cm, green then grey-green to yellow-brown; seeds released 22-24 months after pollination); crop and decay estimated

Saplings are dense, symmetrical, narrow Christmas-tree cones with branch whorls to the ground and upturned branch tips; suppressed under a canopy they persist for decades as stunted, flat-topped umbrellas.
growth.source: Wikipedia (35-55 m; up to 1 m/yr for the first 25 years in good conditions, slowing above 20 m; seed from the 4th decade; lifespan up to 300 years, oldest ring-dated 532; the clonal Old Tjikko root system ~9,550 years); shade tolerance from European silviculture

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (longest spruce cones, 9-17 cm, green or reddish, maturing brown 5-7 months after pollination); erect red female conelets at the crown top in May-June; seed shed over winter, empty cones fall whole later; crop and decay estimated

growth.source: USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (L. sibirica: ~40 m, flowers Apr-May, cones ripen Sep-Nov, seed from 12 yr, good crops every 3-5 yr); Wikipedia (20-50 m; seed-bearing from 10-15 yr; needs full sun; faster-growing than many cold-climate conifers). Height-age curve and longevity estimated.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (female cones 2-5 cm, green flushed red when young, brown when ripe; yellow pollen cones; pollination early spring); USDA WPSM (brownish cones 25-38 mm ripen Sep-Nov). Set, persistence and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: 4-6 short needle-like cotyledons on a thread-thin stem; the first-year seedling is only 2-5 cm tall with a terminal bud. It adds only a few cm a year at first, making a tiny flat-sprayed spire; saplings are narrow, dense, dark-green cones with branches to the ground and can wait for decades under a canopy as advance regeneration.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 1 (Frank, balsam fir): germinates late May-early July after stratification, very shade tolerant, seed from 20-30 yr, 12-18 m (27 m max), lives to about 200 yr, pathological rotation ~70 yr; site-index curves

fruiting.source: USDA Silvics (Frank): flowers late May-June; purple female cones ~25 mm, upright on the top of upper-crown twigs; cones 5-10 cm ripen late Aug-early Sep, scales fall with the seed Sep-Nov leaving the spike; good crops every 2-4 yr, ~134 seeds/cone

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Salix bebbiana (flowers Apr-Jul/Aug with the leaves; bees the chief pollinators; 2-3 million seeds per pound); long-beaked capsules on long stalks (Flora of N America); ripening time, fruit set and crop estimated from Salix

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: tiny oval cotyledons, then a thread-thin green stem with small oval, finely toothed, bright green leaves. Seedlings are rare and grow very slowly; after a few years the plant is a low tuft of sharply angled, bright green, broom-like twigs that stay green through winter after the leaves drop, and rhizomes start sending up new shoots around it.
growth.source: USDA FEIS (Vaccinium myrtillus): 35-64% germination after cold, seedlings rare and initially very slow, seed production begins at about age 3, aerial shoots live up to about 15 yr, rhizomes 23-28 yr, understory dominant in conifer forests with few berries under a closed canopy; Wikipedia: 10-51 cm, can live up to 30 years.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (Vaccinium myrtillus): pink, cream or greenish-white urn to bell flowers borne singly in leaf axils, bees the main pollinators, round dark red to blue-black berries 5-8 mm ripening about 50 days after flowering; Wikipedia: blooms Apr-May, blue-black fruit up to 1 cm Jul-Sep, fruit persists on average 16.7 days. Fruit set and crop estimated.

shrub.silhouette: low tangled shrub of tiny round leaves

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny winged nutlets blow across the snow and sprout in early summer on bare, moist peat or moss. The seedling has two minute oval cotyledons, then small, round, deeply round-toothed leaves on a thin reddish stem; it stays a tiny sprig for years, then branches low and layers into a knee-high spreading mat of wiry brown twigs with coin-sized crinkly leaves that turn red in autumn.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Betula nana (0.15-1 m, slow-growing seedlings, establishment from seed rare, layering and sprouting; 15 d stratification then germination within 14 d at 12 C); Wikipedia (low shade tolerance); growth, first seed and stem ages estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS (monoecious, wind-pollinated, self-incompatible; female catkins in flower early June; male catkins 10-25 mm, female 6-10 mm; seeds ripen in August and disperse from late summer to the next spring, blowing over snow); Wikipedia (fruiting catkins 5-15 mm); counts are catkins, estimated.

shrub.silhouette: low mound of rusty-backed leathery leaves

growth.juvenile_note: Extremely slow start: seedlings on moss are only 2 mm tall after a month and 4 mm after four. Tiny narrow leaves with rolled-under edges become the adult's leathery, strap-like leaves, dark green above and thickly rusty-woolly beneath. It builds a few thin, hairy stems, then spreads by rhizomes and layering into a low, open, aromatic evergreen patch.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Ledum groenlandicum (most seeds germinate in 25-30 days; seedlings 2 mm at 1 month, 4 mm at 4 months; flowers late May-Jul; capsules 4-6 mm ripen in fall; often >50 seeds per flower); Wikipedia (usually 50 cm, rarely 2 m; slow-growing; up to 35 flowers per cluster); ages estimated

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Ledum groenlandicum (flowers late May-Jul; 352 flowers per 100 cm2 in good stands; capsules 4-6 mm ripen in fall; Apis, Bombus and Andrena bees visit); Wikipedia (small white flowers, petals ~1 cm, up to 35 per cluster; mainly bees, also butterflies and beetles; toxic in quantity); set, crop and capsule persistence estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny round cotyledons, then a small flat rosette of narrow willow-like leaves that overwinters; buds form on spreading lateral roots in its first autumn. From the second summer, and each year after, tall unbranched leafy stems rise from the roots and carry magenta spires of flowers, then silky seed-fluff; the stems die back every winter.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Chamerion angustifolium (100% of fresh seed germinated within 10 days; seedlings overwinter as rosettes; flowers Jun-Sep in first or second season; rhizome 6.1 m long at 4 yr; 1-3 m tall; shade intolerant; ~80,000 seeds per plant; stems from rhizomes can bloom within a month)

ground.name: Reindeer lichen

growth.juvenile_note: No seedling: a new patch starts from a broken-off fragment (trampled or carried by wind and reindeer) or, rarely, from spores that must meet a green alga. The young thallus is a scatter of tiny grey stalks that branch in threes and fours, tips all bending one way; over decades they build a springy ash-grey mat up to ~10 cm deep, dying at the base while growing at the tips.
growth.source: Wikipedia Cladonia rangiferina (grows 3-11 mm/yr, 3.9-4.4 mm/yr in Finland; mats to ~10 cm, ~12 cm in humid, 4-6 cm in dry sites; can establish ~2 yr after fire but takes decades to recover; individual lives ~20-30 yr; faster growth in shadier forests)

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators

ground.name: Haircap moss

growth.juvenile_note: Spores germinate on bare, damp, acid soil into a green felt of protonema that buds tiny upright shoots. These grow into stiff, unbranched stems clothed in spreading, narrow, dark green leaves, like miniature spruce seedlings (star-shaped from above, folding up when dry), forming loose to dense turfs that get taller and thicker year by year.
growth.source: Wikipedia Polytrichum commune (stems usually 5-10 cm, often over 30 cm, rarely 70 cm; dioicous with splash-cup males; bogs, wet heath, forest streams and recently disturbed, partly open ground). Growth increments, age at first capsules and turf lifespan estimated.
